findings.element: KPI tiles row — sub-labels and footnote text
findings.detail: The small grey footnote lines beneath each KPI tile (e.g., 'Prior', 'Forecast', range values) are rendered at approximately 7–8 px and are unreadable at normal viewing distance or when printed in a board deck.

findings.element: Sector tiles — commentary body text
findings.detail: The paragraph text inside each sector tile (Passenger Airlines, Hotels & Accommodations, Restaurants & Food Svcs, etc.) is rendered at approximately 6–7 px and is illegible without zooming in, which is unacceptable for a CEO/board audience.

findings.element: 2026 Forecast Scenarios table — 'Key View' and 'As Of' columns
findings.detail: The narrative text in the 'Key View' column for each institution (Goldman Sachs, RSM US, JP Morgan, etc.) is extremely small (~7 px) and cannot be read without magnification, defeating the purpose of including it in a board-level document.

findings.element: Key 2025 Actuals & 2026 Macro Themes — bullet body text
findings.detail: The detailed bullet-point paragraphs at the bottom of the tab are rendered at approximately 6–7 px. At board-deck resolution this section is entirely unreadable.

findings.element: fc-note / outlook commentary block
findings.detail: The blue-bordered commentary paragraph ('Real GDP growth of 2.0% annualized is holding above stall speed…') appears below the KPI tiles and indicator legend row but above the first chart. Visually it sits mid-page rather than unambiguously preceding all chart content; the KPI tiles and indicator strip render above it, meaning the commentary does not precede the first data element on the tab.

findings.element: 2025 Quarterly GDP chart — x-axis label 'Q1 2025'
findings.detail: The leftmost x-axis label appears partially clipped against the left edge of the chart container.

findings.element: 2024 vs 2025 vs 2026F — Key Macro Indicators bar chart
findings.detail: The chart uses three distinct bar colors (dark blue, green/teal, gold) representing 2024 Actual, 2025 Actual, and 2026 Forecast respectively. A legend is shown but at the rendered size the legend labels are illegible, effectively making the series indistinguishable for a reader who cannot zoom in.

findings.element: fc-note commentary block
findings.detail: The commentary block contains hedging language ('could promote', 'could be temporary') and runs to approximately 3 sentences but includes filler qualifiers ('increasingly fragile', 'credible path') that soften rather than assert a clear analytical position, which may violate the forbidden-vocabulary rule.

findings.element: Sector tiles grid — bottom row alignment
findings.detail: The bottom row of sector tiles (Pharmaceuticals/GLP-1, Residential Real Estate, Commercial RE, Auto Manufacturing, Federal Government, Freight & Logistics) appears to have inconsistent tile heights, with some tiles visibly taller than their neighbors, breaking the grid alignment.

findings.element: Sector tiles — top row vs bottom row vertical gap
findings.detail: The vertical gap between the top sector tile row and the bottom sector tile row is noticeably larger than the gap between individual tiles within each row, creating uneven rhythm across the panel grid.

findings.element: Sector panel commentary text (all sector cards)
findings.detail: The per-sector commentary text beneath each mini bar chart is rendered at an extremely small font size (appears ~6-7px), making it unreadable at normal viewing resolution in a board-deck context.

findings.element: Annual chart data vintage / filter bar annotation
findings.detail: The small-print annotation row ('ANNUAL-CHART DATA VINTAGE · FIGURES TO ALPHA AS-OF 2026-03-01 · REFRESH CADENCE: QUARTERLY…') is rendered in very low-contrast gray at ~7px, effectively unreadable.

findings.element: Broad Sector Groups table — source footnote
findings.detail: The sources line beneath the Broad Sector Groups table is rendered at ~6px in light gray, falling below any legible threshold for a CEO-level document.

findings.element: Dashboard-wide footer / data-source strip
findings.detail: The very bottom footer line listing data sources and methodology is rendered at ~6px with low contrast, making it illegible without zooming.

findings.element: KPI tile — 'Debt Service Ratio Q4'20'
findings.detail: The tile label 'DEBT SERVICE RATIO Q4'20' appears clipped on the right edge, and the sub-label text ('% of disp. income / Prior [Q3]') is truncated mid-word within the tile boundary.

findings.element: KPI tile — 'Union Sentiment MAY'26'
findings.detail: Secondary annotation text inside the Union Sentiment tile is cut off at the tile border, with trailing text not fully visible.

findings.element: GDP Commentary — 2025 Growth & 2026 Outlook
findings.detail: The commentary block contains only 2 sentences but one of them is extremely long and compound, effectively embedding hedging qualifiers ('could provide temporary offsets', 'it is weakening'). The phrase 'it is weakening' as a sentence fragment appended with a period reads as an incomplete thought, and 'increasingly fragile' borders on forbidden hedging vocabulary. Verify against style_guide §2 forbidden-word list.

findings.element: Sector card grid — bottom two rows (Airlines/Lodging/Rail/Gaming/Rental Cars row vs. Cruise Lines/Travel Agencies row)
findings.detail: The final row of sector cards (Cruise Lines, Travel Agencies) contains only 2 cards versus the 6-card width of all other rows, leaving a large blank area to the right. While data-driven, the visual gap is jarring and inconsistent with the uniform grid established above it.

findings.element: Sector mini bar charts (multiple panels, e.g., Banking, Insurance, Software/Cloud)
findings.detail: Each sector card displays stacked or grouped colored bars (pink/red/teal/green) across multiple years with no legend identifying what each color represents. A board-level reader cannot determine which color maps to which year or metric without a legend.

findings.element: Sector card status badges — 'Trend Concern' vs. 'Trend Stable' vs. 'Trend Demand'
findings.detail: Several sector cards display status badges in orange, red, green, and blue with label text too small to confirm they map to the style_guide §4 semantic palette (critical=red, warning=orange, confirmed=green). Some badges appear to use non-standard hues (e.g., a blue badge on Airlines) that do not correspond to any documented semantic role.

findings.element: Top KPI tile row — right-most tiles
findings.detail: The rightmost KPI tiles (Union Sentiment, Debt Service Ratio) appear slightly narrower than the tiles to their left, causing inconsistent tile widths across the header row and a compressed appearance for their internal content.

findings.element: Top Sector KPI tile
findings.detail: The 'Top Sector' metric tile displays 'Investmen t Banking' with a visible line break mid-word, truncating/wrapping 'Investment' incorrectly and making it appear as two words across lines.

findings.element: Source footnotes below all charts
findings.detail: Source citation text at the bottom of the Monthly Wage Growth chart, the Annual History chart, and the sector table is rendered at an extremely small font size (appears to be ~6-7px), making it effectively unreadable at normal viewing scale for a board-level audience.

findings.element: Footer / data provenance line at very bottom of dashboard
findings.detail: The full-width footer line at the very bottom of the page is rendered at an illegibly small size, well below the minimum body text threshold for a CEO-grade deck.

findings.element: Avg Hourly Earnings by Sector bar chart — Y-axis sector labels
findings.detail: Several sector name labels on the left Y-axis of the 'Avg Hourly Earnings by Sector — 2025 vs 2024' horizontal bar chart appear compressed and nearly overlapping each other, reducing legibility for a board audience.

findings.element: Wage Growth Commentary — Nominal vs Real (fc-note block)
findings.detail: The commentary paragraph is a single very long run-on sentence that exceeds the 4-sentence maximum and contains hedging language ('ambiguous', 'may reflect', 'does not yet justify') which is flagged as forbidden hedging filler under the style guide.

findings.element: Wage Growth Commentary block
findings.detail: While the commentary does appear above the charts, it is separated from the first chart by a row of KPI summary tiles and a data-vintage footnote block, which may violate the requirement that the fc-note directly precedes the first chart without intervening non-commentary elements.

findings.element: Wage Growth by Sector table — 'Falling' trend badges
findings.detail: Every single row in the sector table shows a red 'Falling' badge, including the 'All Private' summary row. If 'Falling' is mapped to the 'critical' semantic color, having it applied uniformly to all 18 rows with no 'warning' or neutral differentiation suggests either a data error or a color-role misapplication where the critical color is overused, diluting its signal value.

findings.element: Inflation Breadth — Trimmed-Mean & Median CPI vs Headline (bottom chart)
findings.detail: The chart area is almost entirely blank with a prominent 'AWAITING FIRST PIPELINE RUN' placeholder message visible in the center. No data is plotted despite three legend series being defined (Headline CPI MoM, Trimmed-Mean CPI, Median CPI). This would be highly embarrassing in a board deck.

findings.element: Inflation Breadth chart — pipeline status overlay
findings.detail: The text 'AWAITING FIRST PIPELINE RUN' is displayed as a watermark/overlay inside the chart panel, indicating the data pipeline has not yet executed. This is a placeholder state that should never appear in a published dashboard.

findings.element: Inflation Breadth — Trimmed-Mean & Median CPI vs Headline (bottom chart)
findings.detail: The few visible line segments at the far right of the chart appear disconnected and do not form a continuous series across the full 24-month window described in the subtitle. The bulk of the chart area has no plotted lines.

findings.element: Annual CPI bar chart — x-axis year labels
findings.detail: The year labels along the x-axis of the 'U.S. CPI Inflation — Annual Rate (Dec-to-Dec YoY %)' chart are extremely small and difficult to read at normal viewing size, making it hard to identify individual years in the series.

findings.element: CPI by Category — MoM Change bar chart — bar value labels
findings.detail: The percentage labels on the horizontal bars in the 'CPI by Category — MoM Change (Apr'26 vs Mar'26)' chart are very small and low-contrast against the bar fill colors, making them difficult to read without zooming in.

findings.element: Monthly CPI Headline vs Core YoY line chart — data point annotations
findings.detail: Several inline data labels on the 13-month trend line chart appear to crowd together in the right portion of the chart (around Feb–Apr 2026), with values and leader lines overlapping or very close together, reducing readability.

findings.element: Footer / source attribution text across all charts
findings.detail: Source lines beneath each chart (e.g., 'SOURCE: BLS CPI-U ALL URBAN CONSUMERS…') are rendered at an extremely small font size, well below a readable threshold for a board-level presentation.

findings.element: CPI Commentary — Inflation Trajectory & Fed Implications
findings.detail: The commentary block contains hedging language ('risk re-acceleration', 'not yet fully reflected') and runs as a single dense paragraph that is difficult to parse quickly. It also uses the phrase 'rate relief is not imminent' which borders on editorial opinion rather than factual summary, potentially violating the forbidden-vocabulary clause.

findings.element: Bottom section — Inflation Breadth chart panel vs upper chart panels
findings.detail: The vertical spacing between the 'CPI Category Annual Rates' table / 'CPI by Category 2022 Peak' chart row and the 'Inflation Breadth' panel below appears noticeably larger than the spacing between the upper chart panels, creating an inconsistent rhythm on the tab.
